field_guide.cik: Company identifier stored as text. Join filings using both CIK and accession number.
field_guide.fact_name: Raw XBRL concept. Related concepts may have different definitions.
field_guide.fact_category: Taxonomy namespace. Compare concepts only under compatible definitions.
field_guide.fact_value: Value in the returned unit. NULL is missing and never implies zero.
field_guide.unit: Original units. USD values are unscaled dollars.
field_guide.end_date: Fact period end. It can precede the filing's fiscal year.
field_guide.fiscal_year: Fiscal-year label of the disclosure. Verify the fact's actual end_date.
field_guide.fiscal_period: Source fiscal-period label. Check period length and frame for flows.
field_guide.frame: Supplementary period indicator. A missing frame does not establish annual duration.
field_guide.filed_date: Submission date, distinct from the fact period end.
field_guide.form_type: Source filing form. One period may be disclosed in several filings.
field_guide.accession_number: SEC submission identifier. A matching filings row may be absent.
field_guide.dimension_segment: Segment scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.
field_guide.dimension_geography: Geographic scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.

hits.text: Deferred tax assets represent amounts available to reduce income taxes payable on taxable income in future years. Such assets arise because of temporary differences between the financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities, as well as from net operating loss and tax credit carryforwards. We evaluate the recoverability of these future tax deductions and credits by assessing the adequacy of future expected taxable income from all sources, including future growth, forecasted earnings, future taxable income, the mix of earnings in the jurisdictions in which we operate, historical earnings, taxable income in prior years, if carryback is permitted under the law, carryforward periods and prudent and feasible tax planning strategies. A valuation allowance is established if it is more likely than not that all or a portion of the deferred tax asset will not be realized. To the extent sufficient positive evidence becomes available, we may release all or a portion of our valuation allowance in one or more future periods. A release of the valuation allowance, if any, would result in the recognition of certain deferred tax assets and a material income tax benefit for the period in which such release is recorded.

hits.text: We use the asset and liability method of accounting for income taxes, in which deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the consolidated financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases. We measure deferred tax assets and liabilities using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be reversed. We recognize the effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates within the provision for income taxes as income and expense in the period that includes the enactment date. A valuation allowance is established if it is more likely than not that all or a portion of the deferred tax asset will not be realized. In determining the need for a valuation allowance, we consider future growth, forecasted earnings, forecasted taxable income, the mix of earnings in the jurisdictions in which we operate, historical earnings, taxable income in prior years, if carryback is permitted under the law, carryforward periods and prudent and feasible tax planning strategies.

arguments: {"sql": "SELECT id, fact_name, fact_value, unit, fiscal_year, end_date, form_type, accession_number FROM financial_facts WHERE cik='1373715' AND (fact_name LIKE '%Depreciation%' OR fact_name LIKE '%IncomeTaxExpense%' OR fact_name LIKE '%NetIncomeLoss%') AND end_date IN ('2024-12-31','2023-12-31') ORDER BY fact_name, end_date LIMIT 40", "params": []}

field_guide.fact_name: Raw XBRL concept. Related concepts may have different definitions.
field_guide.fact_value: Value in the returned unit. NULL is missing and never implies zero.
field_guide.unit: Original units. USD values are unscaled dollars.
field_guide.fiscal_year: Fiscal-year label of the disclosure. Verify the fact's actual end_date.
field_guide.end_date: Fact period end. It can precede the filing's fiscal year.
field_guide.form_type: Source filing form. One period may be disclosed in several filings.
field_guide.accession_number: SEC submission identifier. A matching filings row may be absent.

interpretation_notes: Check end_date, fiscal_period, frame and form_type before comparing flows across periods.
Check concept, unit, period length and dimensions before identifying repeats.
Repeated disclosures can reflect revisions. Retain fact IDs and accession numbers and do not sum repeats.
Do not conflate net income, parent-attributable income, operating income and pretax income.

sources.sql: SELECT id, fact_name, fact_value, unit, fiscal_year, end_date, form_type, accession_number FROM financial_facts WHERE cik='1373715' AND (fact_name LIKE '%Depreciation%' OR fact_name LIKE '%IncomeTaxExpense%' OR fact_name LIKE '%NetIncomeLoss%') AND end_date IN ('2024-12-31','2023-12-31') ORDER BY fact_name, end_date LIMIT 40

projected_provenance.basis: Values projected by the supplied SELECT, not inferred source lineage.

message.content:
Yes — the FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, accession 0001373715-25-000010, local file data/filings/1373715/now-20241231.htm) highlights several notable accounting matters and adjustments:

**1. Change in accounting estimate — data center equipment useful life (the largest P&L adjustment)**
In January 2024 the company extended the estimated useful life of data center equipment from four to five years, effective fiscal 2024. Based on the carrying amount at December 31, 2023, the effect for the year ended December 31, 2024 was a **$101 million reduction in depreciation expense** and an **$81 million increase in net income ($0.39 per basic and diluted share)**. This is a prospective change in estimate, not an error correction. (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:231127; also referenced at :173003)

**2. Revision of prior-period financial statements — cash flow misclassification (immaterial error)**
During Q2 2024 the company identified an immaterial error in the March 31, 2024 condensed consolidated statement of cash flows: the **second installment payment of $184 million** for a business combination completed in Q3 2023 was misclassified as an investing cash outflow instead of a financing cash outflow. Management concluded it was not material to any previously issued financial statements and said it would revise the error in the Form 10-Q for the three months ending March 31, 2025. (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:257667, under "Revision of Prior Period Financial Statements")

**3. New accounting pronouncement adopted**
ASU 2023-07 (Segment Reporting — Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures) was adopted effective January 1, 2024 on a **retrospective basis**, expanding segment expense disclosures. (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:258442)

**4. Tax-related items (context for comparability)**
The prior year included a large non-recurring tax benefit: a **$1.05 billion release of valuation allowance** in 2023, producing a **$723 million income tax benefit** for 2023 (IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit fact ID 1342046/1342047, −$723M) versus **$313 million of income tax expense** in 2024 (fact ID 1342056). A valuation allowance was still maintained at December 31, 2024 (notably for California). This is a disclosed item, not an adjustment to prior statements, but it materially affects year-over-year comparability of net income ($1,731M in 2023 vs. $1,425M in 2024; fact IDs 1344906/1344916).

**5. Critical audit matter and critical estimates**
The auditor's sole critical audit matter was **revenue recognition for subscription revenue** (chunk :216865, :217670). Critical accounting estimates also include purchase-price allocation for business combinations (intangible fair values, with measurement-period adjustments to goodwill permitted up to one year) and valuation allowances on deferred tax assets. No goodwill impairment was disclosed; the report describes only the impairment-testing policy.

**Limitations:** Figures above are as disclosed in the FY2024 10-K text; the $101M/$81M useful-life effect and the $184M reclassification are company-disclosed amounts (the latter is a planned revision, not yet reflected in the bundled statements). The structured database contains only one annual report snapshot for this CIK, so I could not independently verify the later 10-Q revision.
